blueprint.narrative: Designed for the cold high-altitude environment of Leh, this shelter prioritizes low-cost thermal performance and durability. A southern airlock foyer and main living area maximize passive solar gain into high-mass stone floors while northern bedrooms and utility spaces act as a cold-weather thermal buffer zone. EPS panel walls integrated with cement plaster offer structural rigidity and superior R-value performance on a strict budget. Cross-ventilation pathways leverage natural stack effect through roof-level vents to maintain air freshness without substantial temperature loss.
